findings_addressed.oracle: text.rfind('} finally {') gives the byte offset of the outermost finally block opener; text.rfind(stopped_call) gives the byte offset of the last -State 'stopped' call; the structural position assert stopped_pos > finally_pos is an independent positional oracle computed without injecting any data into the script.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In any of the four monitor scripts (e.g. dll_monitor.ps1), move `Write-DllLifecycle -State 'stopped' ...` from inside the `} finally {` block to a position *before* the `} finally {` marker (e.g. place it just before the `try {` that wraps the main loop) — the new `assert stopped_pos > finally_pos` assertion will FAIL because stopped_pos < finally_pos.

notes: The existing source-text scan correctly detected absence of the lifecycle calls but could not verify their structural position. The hardening adds two positional assertions using rfind(): (1) the outermost '} finally {' marker must exist, and (2) the last '-State stopped' call must appear after it in the file. This closes the dead-code-branch gap identified in G0049 for all four parametrized monitors without requiring a Windows runtime. All four quality checks pass with zero findings. POST-WORKFLOW FIX (2026-06-23): a pre-existing sibling test (test_start_monitors_skips_underscore_prefixed_scripts, NOT a finding, untouched by the fixer) timed out at the 60s container cap. Root cause: its monitor.ps1/_helper.ps1 fixtures did Start-Sleep -Seconds 300, and start_monitors.cmd launches them via Start-Process with inheritable handles, so run(capture_output=True) blocked on the inherited pipe until the 300s monitors exited. The monitors.pids file is written at launch (not at monitor exit), so the long sleep was unnecessary. Reduced both sleeps to 10s; run() now returns promptly, the filter assertion (helper skipped, monitor tracked) is unchanged. Verified GREEN in sandbox.
